n1.text: You return a novel at {library}. As it is stamped, a folded note slips out: "Chapter three made me laugh out loud. I hope it does the same for you." There is no name, only a tiny drawing of a teapot.

n2.text: Jack turns the note over in his careful hands. "Good paper. Thick, cream, a little rough at the edge. That's the kind kept on the writing desk in {kingHall}." He hands it back, looking rather pleased with himself.

choices.label: Ask Robin for a second opinion

n3.text: Robin holds the note up to a lantern, then produces a teacup from nowhere. "The teapot is a signature! Whoever drew it loves a quiet cuppa. Try {kingHall} or {queenParlour}, where the kettle never cools."

choices.label: Write a reply and leave it

n5.text: King Kenny reads the note and goes pink to the ears. "Guilty," he says. "I've tucked little notes into library books for years. I never thought one would be followed all the way to {kingHall}."

choices.label: Ask to see his other notes
Suggest writing a new one together

n6.text: Queen Rose studies the teapot and smiles. "Not mine, though I'd be proud of it. That wobbly spout is Kenny's. He thinks nobody knows." She pours you a cup while she speaks.

n7.text: Back at {library}, you write underneath: "Chapter three was a delight. Thank you." You tuck it into the book and set it on the returns shelf. Some mysteries are nicest left warm and unsolved.

n8.text: Kenny opens a drawer full of tiny teapot notes, each waiting for a book. "Take your pick," he says. You choose one about a lost umbrella, and the two of you laugh until the tea goes cold.

n9.text: You and Kenny write a note together, arguing happily over every word. At {library} you slip it into a fresh book and leave it on the shelf. Someone will find it soon, and you'll both pretend not to watch.

n10.text: The tea is warm and the cushions are deep. Rose tells you Kenny's notes have cheered half the town. You sit a while longer in {queenParlour}, in no hurry at all, with the book open on your knee.
